<reason>CON built a consistent fork (sex field is either a checkable fact or an unverifiable self-report) and then turned PRO's own concessions—no biology, no medical content, officers match face/photo/number—into the claim that the field is inert, so the honest fix is deletion rather than expansion. CON also gave a coherent account of "checkable" (origin record) and exposed the circularity of X-vouches-for-X, and answered PRO's deletion question directly with the race/religion analogy. PRO's best material—the "second look that resolves itself" versus a mismatch that reads as deception, the surname-change analogy, and the late point that deletion leaves passports and visa forms binary—kept a live route open, and CON never squarely handled why deletion works for passports where a sex field is standard. But PRO's passport point arrived thin and late, PRO never pressed that amended M/F markers for trans people already break CON's origin-record test, and PRO's "330 million / maximal coercion" framing was weaker than CON's "a field disappears, the citizen does not." CON's two clipped turns are a real execution cost, but CON still made the decisive comparison cleaner and more memorable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A1/inert-field turn in Rebuttal 2 and closing: quoting PRO that identification runs "by photo, number, name and birthdate, not by matching sex letters," then arguing PRO had spent three speeches proving the field does no identifying work before demanding the state expand it—"you remove decoration; you do not expand it." PRO's reply that F on an androgynous person manufactures suspicion was solid but CON's counter that deletion relieves that mismatch for more people, including androgynous cis people, blunted it.</best_rebuttal>
